title: introduce-multivariant-adaptive-threshold-canary
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Adds a multi-variant performance canary workflow that supports adaptive thresholds per-route and per-model, implements statistical-significance based regression detection, and integrates with the rollout controller to automatically pause or rollback releases. Motivation: previous single-threshold canaries generated noisy alerts for heterogeneous traffic patterns and missed subtle regressions when traffic mixes multiple models or routes. This change provides stricter signal isolation for canaries that exercise different model variants or sequence-length distributions and reduces manual intervention by surfacing actionable regressions with confidence scores.
commits: Initial implementation: add canary controller and metrics ingestion adapters
Add adaptive-threshold estimator using sliding-window percentile and Welch's t-test for significance
Integrate with rollout API: pause/rollback hooks and annotated decisions
Add canary e2e job and synthetic traffic generator for multi-variant scenarios
Tests: unit tests for estimator, integration tests for rollout pause path, performance harness baseline fixtures
Docs: runbook and observability notes for oncall
files_changed: perf-canary/controller/canary_controller.go - new controller coordinating experiments and decisions
perf-canary/estimator/adaptive_threshold.go - adaptive threshold logic and statistical tests
perf-canary/ingest/prom_adapter.go - normalize prom metrics into estimator format
console/pages/canaries/overview.tsx - UI to show per-variant baselines and confidence
charts/alerts/canary-regression.yaml - alert rules that include confidence and suppressed windows
ci/workflows/perf-canary-e2e.yaml - new e2e job using synthetic traffic
review_comments: Diego Rivera: Left a comment on adaptive_threshold.go: prefer using an online variance estimator to reduce memory pressure when sliding window size is large. Also request clearer invariants for sample alignment.
Aisha Kaur: Responded: switched to Welford's online variance for window aggregates; added comments and micro-benchmarks in estimator_test.go.
Samir Patel: Noted that the alert rule raw threshold should not be removed until we validate historical false-positive rate. Requested a feature flag for the adaptive estimator.
Aisha Kaur: Added feature flag perf.canary.use_adaptive_threshold (default true in staging, false in prod) and a migration plan in the runbook.
Lena Fischer: Verified the rollout pause path and asked to include telemetry for decision rationale in traces. Requested an example in the console showing per-variant baselines.
Aisha Kaur: Added decision rationale as structured annotations on rollout events and added console example screenshot and description in docs.
release_notes: Introduce multi-variant perf canary with adaptive thresholds and automated rollout guards. Adds estimator with statistical tests for regression detection, rollout pause/rollback hooks, and a synthetic multi-variant e2e job. Feature flag perf.canary.use_adaptive_threshold governs rollout.
files_changed_high_level_snippets: canary_controller.go: decision flow evaluates variants independently then synthesizes global action via conservative OR across variants
hooks.go: PauseOnRegression(ctx, rolloutID, reason) annotated with confidence and metric samples
manual_test_instructions: Run ci/workflows/perf-canary-e2e.yaml locally: start synthetic_multi_variant_generator with --variants=3 --seq-dist=short,mid,long and point to staging Prometheus, then create a canary rollout targeting canary controller and assert the controller emits PauseOnRegression when latency regressions exceed adaptive thresholds for two consecutive windows.
operational_notes: Default adaptive estimator enabled in staging; monitor canaries/canary_regression_alarm for confidence>0.95. If noisy alerts occur, increase sliding_window_seconds or enable sample suppression for low-volume variants. Rollout decisions are annotated under rollout_events in traces and include the rationale field.
observability_changes: Added metrics: canary_estimator_baseline_p90, canary_estimator_baseline_p99, canary_estimator_confidence, canary_decision_count{action,pause,rollback}. Added logs at INFO for decisions and DEBUG for per-sample alignments.
security_implications: No secrets introduced. Access control required for rollout hooks is enforced by existing rollout service RBAC. Audit logs capture decision events.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1376: Evaluate historical canary noise after 2 weeks of traffic
ENG-1377: Backfill historical baselines for critical routes to evaluate threshold drift
ENG-1399: Expose per-variant baseline export for external analysis
notes_on_uniqueness: This PR focuses on multi-variant isolation and adaptive thresholds rather than per-route static thresholds or simple feedback loops; it introduces statistical-significance-driven decisions and integrates reason-annotated rollout actions to reduce manual rollbacks.
